solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Elector all at sea?

parts.note: a voter who is all at sea is undecided, drifting between parties rather than anchored to one

explanation.surface: A voter lost on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All at sea' pretends to be nautical; it means undecided, and a voter not tied to a party is said to float.
explanation.definitionFit: An undecided voter whose support is not fixed to any party is described with this phrase in election coverage.

clue.text: It's not bound to be distributed

definitions.text: It's not bound to be distributed

parts.words: It's not bound to be distributed
parts.note: a single printed sheet with no binding, made to be handed out

explanation.surface: Something free of obligation is going to be shared out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not bound' reads as 'not obliged'; here it means not stitched into a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A handout is an unbound printed sheet given out in quantity, which is exactly what the clue describes.

clue.text: Open with a shock

definitions.meaning: a jar is a jolt or shock, so 'with a jar'

explanation.surface: Opening something and getting a fright.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly open describes a door left unlatched; split in two it reads as 'a jolt'.

clue.text: Means to stop and isn't worried about it

indicators.note: the scrambled letters wrap around the word for stop, which is what 'it' refers back to
worried means agitated, so the letters of the word are shaken into a new order

parts.note: to stop is to end

explanation.surface: Someone plans to halt and is unbothered by doing so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to the stop, so it is the stopping word that the scrambled letters go 'about'; 'Means' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To intend is to mean to do something, so 'means' as a verb is a synonym.

clue.text: A beggar sorting out contents of bins

indicators.note: sorting out suggests putting things in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tramp rummaging through rubbish bins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorting out' rearranges A BEGGAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish is what fills dustbins, so the contents of bins is a fair description.

clue.text: Evict some impecunious tenants

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A landlord throwing out tenants who cannot pay.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw someone out of a place is a plain synonym of evict.

clue.text: Land on a site needing development

indicators.note: a plot needing development will be reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A building plot waiting to be developed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing development' rearranges ON A SITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Baltic state is a country, and 'land' is a common word for a country.

clue.text: Show jumper seen in the gym

definitions.text: Show jumper seen in the gym

parts.words: Show jumper seen in the gym
parts.note: a showjumper is a horse; the gym version is the padded apparatus vaulted over

explanation.surface: A competition horse turning up in a gymnasium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show jumper' points to equestrian events; the gymnastics apparatus is called a horse and is jumped over.
explanation.definitionFit: The gymnastics apparatus that athletes leap over is named after a horse.

clue.text: Expectant mother?

parts.note: a woman expecting a baby could jokingly be said to be a lady who is waiting

explanation.surface: A pregnant woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The real sense is a royal attendant; 'expectant' is taken literally as waiting.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen's female attendant has this title, which can be read whimsically as a woman waiting for a birth.

clue.text: Girl meets chap, starts talking, but is unyielding

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name
a chap is a man

indicators.note: starts takes only the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A girl meets a man who begins chatting, yet she will not budge.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone firm and refusing to give way is unyielding; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: The stone archaeologists treat so cryptically

indicators.note: cryptically signals that the words are disguised, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Archaeologists handling a famous stone with coded writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptically' rearranges TREAT SO; the Rosetta Stone let scholars read hieroglyphs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rosetta Stone is the inscribed slab archaeologists used to decipher Egyptian hieroglyphs.

clue.text: Three students seen around university in break

indicators.note: the three letters are seen placed round the next piece

parts.note: L for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate, used three times

explanation.surface: Three students on a university break.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner plate on British cars, so a student; three of them go round U.
explanation.definitionFit: A lull is a pause or quiet spell, so 'break' is a synonym.

clue.text: Insert in ballad

parts.note: a lay is a narrative song or ballad

explanation.surface: A verse slipped into a ballad.
explanation.definitionFit: An inlay is something set into a surface, so an insert.

clue.text: Grudging admiration of diplomat who lacks nothing

indicators.note: the diplomat is missing a piece, so it is removed from his title

parts.note: an envoy is a diplomat
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A diplomat with nothing to his name looks on others with grudging respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who lacks' removes O (nothing) from ENVOY.
explanation.definitionFit: Coveting what another has while admiring it is the feeling of jealousy, a grudging admiration.

clue.text: It's hard hit when ironworkers strike

definitions.text: It's hard hit when ironworkers strike

parts.words: It's hard hit when ironworkers strike
parts.note: strike means hammer, not walk out; the smith's iron block takes the blows

explanation.surface: Something suffers badly during an industrial strike by metalworkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' looks like industrial action and 'hard hit' like suffering; the blacksmith's block is literally hard and hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith's iron block on which hot metal is hammered is literally hard and hit.

clue.text: Ship's rigging in boxes

definitions.meaning: the masts, booms and yards of a ship
boxes as a verb, fights practice rounds

explanation.surface: A ship's rigging packed in crates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxes' looks like a noun for containers; it is the verb for sparring.
explanation.definitionFit: Masts and yards are poles of the rigging, and to box in practice is to spar.

clue.text: Gives voice and breaks tension

indicators.note: breaks suggests the word is split apart and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone speaks up and relieves a tense atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' rearranges TENSION.
explanation.definitionFit: To intone is to speak or chant in a level voice, so to give voice.

clue.text: Account for what is no longer clear

parts.note: ex means former, no longer so
plain means clear

explanation.surface: Justifying something that has become murky.
explanation.definitionFit: To account for something is to give the reasons for it, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Alpine flower

parts.note: flower read as a thing that flows; a slow river of ice in the Alps

explanation.surface: A mountain bloom such as edelweiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is not a bloom but something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow-moving mass of ice in a mountain valley flows downhill, so it is a flower in the Alps.

clue.text: Acquit a drunk, now living on water

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are staggering about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A court clears a drunk, who now lives on a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges ACQUIT A; 'a drunk' reads as a drunkard.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that lives in or on water is aquatic by definition.

clue.text: Acquires lots of money — like a croupier does?

definitions.meaning: a croupier draws chips in with a rake

explanation.surface: Someone getting rich, like a casino dealer gathering chips.
explanation.definitionFit: Earning money in large amounts is an idiom from the croupier's rake gathering stakes.

clue.text: A bitter brew that might go to father's head

definitions.text: that might go to father's head

indicators.note: to brew is to mix up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A pint of bitter that goes to a priest's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brew' rearranges A BITTER; 'go to father's head' looks like getting drunk, but 'father' is a Catholic priest wearing a square cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A biretta is the square cap worn by Catholic priests, addressed as Father, so it sits on his head.

clue.text: Profit from charity performance

definitions.meaning: a concert held to raise money for a cause

explanation.surface: Making money from a charity show.
explanation.definitionFit: Gain or advantage is a benefit, and a fundraising show is also called a benefit.

clue.text: Labels for matches

definitions.meaning: tags or tickets used to identify things

explanation.surface: Labels for boxes of matches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'matches' looks like the fire-lighting noun; it is the verb 'corresponds'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tally means a label or tag, and as a verb, to correspond, so 'labels' and 'matches' both fit.

clue.text: So backward about turning up for work

indicators.note: the first reversed word goes around the second
backward means the word so is read from the end
turning means the word up is flipped round

explanation.surface: A slow composer who turns up for work late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' makes OS, 'turning' makes PU, and 'about' puts PU inside OS.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or artistic work, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: This one's a real stinker!

parts.note: a stinker is normally a nasty thing or a hard puzzle; here it is an animal that literally stinks

explanation.surface: Something truly awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stinker' is slang for a rotten thing; taken literally it is the smelly black-and-white animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The black-and-white mammal that sprays a foul smell is literally a stinker.

clue.text: Plan to put a pound in the kitty

indicators.note: in places the pound symbol inside the kitty

parts.note: the pot is the pool of money in a card game
L is the abbreviation for pound (libra)

explanation.surface: Putting a pound into the shared pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kitty' is a pool of stakes, not a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot is a scheme or plan, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Look up to observe

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a peek is a look

explanation.surface: Glancing upward to watch something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PEEK in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep a rule or custom is to observe it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: A king on way up to be an emperor

indicators.note: on places the reversed way before the letters that follow
in a down clue, up means the word for way is read upwards

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
R is for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king rising to become an emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the turned way sits on top of A and the king.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of the Russian emperor is a synonym of emperor.

clue.text: They won't stand for being models

definitions.text: They won't stand for being models

parts.words: They won't stand for being models
parts.note: won't stand for reads as refuse to tolerate; really, artists' models who stay seated

explanation.surface: People refusing to put up with being used as models.
explanation.walkthrough: 'won't stand for' looks like 'won't tolerate'; really it means they pose seated.
explanation.definitionFit: People who pose for a portrait while seated are the artist's models.

clue.text: Create trend

explanation.surface: Starting a new craze.
explanation.definitionFit: To shape something is to make it, and a vogue in clothes is a style or trend.

clue.text: Needle-worker found in practice

parts.note: needle-worker suggests a seamstress; practice is a clinic, where needles are put into patients

explanation.surface: A seamstress at work in her studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needle-worker' suggests sewing; 'practice' is a medical practice using needles for therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: A therapist who inserts fine needles into the body works with needles in a practice.
